messages:
Maya: opsbot posted a big alert stream — ~1.2k failed s3 writes from backup-svc in the last 2h, spiking our SIEM. Anyone seen this?
opsbot: [ALERT] 1200x s3:PutObject failed — service_account=backup-svc job=nightly-backup region=us-west-2 (https://alerts.example.com/evt/12345)
Adrian: yep, backup team rolled a change that made retries more aggressive. It's expected but noisy.
Kevin: we should suppress these from generating incidents but keep raw events for 90d. Agree?
Maya: propose rule: suppress alerts for service_account=backup-svc unless > 50 failures in 5m. Enrich events with job_id/run_id. Draft rule:
```
rule_id: reduce-backup-noise
conditions: event.type == "s3:PutObject" and event.service_account == "backup-svc"
aggregation: count(event) over 5m
trigger_threshold: 50
action: suppress_alerts_below_threshold; tag="suppressed:backup-noise"
```
Adrian: +1. Make sure we still surface auth failures or permission-denied types.
Jen (SRE): can you add a dashboard showing suppressed vs triggered? need to watch if threshold hides real issues.
Maya: will implement rule and dashboard. Will also add enrichment keys. ETA today EOD.
Kevin: I'll update retention/archival policy to ensure suppressed logs stay searchable for 90 days.
Jen (SRE): I'll add a monitor for distinct source IPs and job_id entropy; if that jumps, we escalate regardless of suppression.
Adrian: any change to alert routing? ops team wants no pages for suppressed events.
Maya: yes — suppressed events won't page, they go to SIEM index + suppressed tag and a weekly digest. Urgent events still page.
opsbot: Rule deployment queued: change-request #BR-842, awaiting review by security. (:eyes:)
Kevin: I'll review the CR now.
Maya: quick follow-up — keep note for post-incident: add a short-runbook explaining when to disable suppression (permission denied on majority, or >5 distinct job_ids failing).
Jen (SRE): adding runbook entry.
Adrian: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
